name: Zolpidem + Melatonin
meta: Zolpidem Tartrate: Non-benzodiazepine hypnotic (imidazopyridine, 'Z-drug'); Melatonin: Melatonin receptor agonist (chronobiotic hypnotic)

Psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985 and Schedule H/H1 of the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules; Melatonin: Prescription medicine in India (Schedule H for tablet formulations; verify current listing)
sections: White to off-white crystalline powder (tartrate); melting point 193–197 °C; sparingly soluble in water.
Pale yellow/white crystalline powder; melting point 117 °C.

Zolpidem Tartrate: Generic since 2007; the most widely prescribed 'Z-drug' hypnotic. Onset ~30 minutes after an oral tablet. First approval/introduction: Europe 1988 (Synthélabo); US FDA 1992 (Searle). Melatonin: Discovered in 1958 by Aaron Lerner; use for circadian rhythm disorders patented in 1987 (Monash University) and as a sleep aid in 1995 (MIT). First approval/introduction: Prolonged-release melatonin EU 2007 (Neurim Pharmaceuticals).
Zolpidem rapidly induces sleep via GABA-A alpha-1 receptors; melatonin supports circadian re-alignment and sleep quality, potentially allowing better sleep architecture.

Zolpidem Tartrate Selective agonist at the alpha-1 subunit-containing GABA-A receptors (benzodiazepine-1 site), producing hypnotic effect with little anxiolytic, muscle-relaxant or anticonvulsant activity. Receptor / target profile: Positive allosteric modulator selective for alpha-1-containing GABA-A receptors (Ki ~27 nM), producing hypnotic effect with weak anxiolytic/myorelaxant activity.

Melatonin Endogenous pineal hormone that acts on MT1 and MT2 receptors in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, promoting sleep onset and re-synchronising circadian rhythm. Receptor / target profile: Agonist at MT1 and MT2 receptors in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, regulating the circadian clock and sleep–wake cycle.
Summary: Bioavailability ~70%; rapid onset (Tmax ~1.6 h; slower with food). ~92% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4. Half-life ~2.5 h (longer in elderly/hepatic impairment).
Summary: Rapidly absorbed; bioavailability ~15% (first-pass). Tmax ~1 h. Metabolised by CYP1A2 to 6-hydroxymelatonin. Half-life 40–60 min (immediate release).
Short-term treatment of insomnia, especially with difficulty initiating sleep and disturbed circadian rhythm

Zolpidem Tartrate: Complex sleep behaviours; next-morning alertness; dependence.
Zolpidem Tartrate: Somnolence to coma, respiratory depression. Supportive care; flumazenil may reverse. Melatonin: Drowsiness; supportive care. Clearance within ~12 h.
Evidence derives from component trials; no large randomised trials of the fixed combination.
